critical_failures: Cites identifiers (TG-035, RT-035, WH-035), an inline receipt, and a 08:10 UTC receipt time that are not in the visible events; the attachments list is empty and event-001 has no readable content.
Presents warehouse confirmation of physical receipt as established fact, though only the customer's claim is visible.
judgment.explanation: The proposal is an internal operator review. That is a sensible and conservative route, since no refunds-team contact is visible. It asks the operator to establish a verified route before forwarding anything. It also says receipt is not refund approval and asks only for a review reference and next update date, so it makes no unauthorized commitment. The main problem is grounding. The visible events are a customer message saying the warehouse has the return and that no refund review exists (event-002), and a warehouse email whose body is unavailable (event-001). The identifiers TG-035, RT-035 and WH-035, the 'inline warehouse receipt', and the '08:10 UTC' receipt time appear in neither event. The attachments list is empty, so no receipt is visible. The 08:10 time also doesn't match the visible timestamps, which are 09:00 and 09:10 UTC. The statement that 'Receiving confirms physical receipt' rests only on the customer's claim and an unreadable warehouse email. The proposal also leaves out the visible customer name (Melli Orven) and the customer's actual request, which is to pass the receipt to the team that handles refund review. The overall step is right, but its factual details are unsupported.
